reports.subject: film
reports.headline: “Sister Brother Manhole Cover”, by Milcho Manchevski, wins the Tokyo Grand Prix; Lisandro Alonso takes best director
reports.deck: The 39th Tokyo International Film Festival has closed with its awards: the Balkan dramatic comedy takes the top prize, Hu Ling and Narita Ryo the acting awards, and Mohammad Rasoulof and O Mipo the Kurosawa Akira Award.
paragraphs: The jury of the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival gave the Tokyo Grand Prix (the Governor of Tokyo Award) to “Sister Brother Manhole Cover”, by Milcho Manchevski, a co-production of North Macedonia, Bulgaria, Serbia, Albania, Italy and the UK. Producer Jane Kortoshev accepted it on his behalf, and the jury praised its blend of humour, tragedy and drama. Trade coverage of its international sales describes it as the story of two orphaned siblings who live off stolen manhole covers and bronze statues; we found no review.

The rest of the competition: Special Jury Prize to “Magic Atlas” (Singapore), by Sun Xun; best director to Lisandro Alonso for “Double Freedom” (Chile, Argentina, Luxembourg, Germany and the UK); best actress to Hu Ling in “The Night That Binds Us” (France and Hong Kong); best actor to Narita Ryo in “Two Cigarettes, Three Nights” (Japan), accepted by director Mishima Yukiko; best artistic contribution to Jelena Maksimović's “Until the Day Ends”, for its cinematography; and the Audience Award to Teodora Ana Mihai's “Heysel 85”.

In the side sections, Asian Future honoured Tareq Daoud's “Serife Tavsan” (the winners page prints the title as the director's name; we follow the ceremony report), and Nippon Cinema Now honoured Tanaka Miki's “silver express”. The Ethical Film Award went to “I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming”. The ceremony took place on 4 November at Hulic Hall Tokyo.

The Kurosawa Akira Award, worth one million yen to each recipient, was presented the night before at the Imperial Hotel to Japanese director O Mipo and Iran's Mohammad Rasoulof, whom the committee praised for his uncompromising look at injustice and oppression. None of the winning films has a Spanish release date we can verify yet.

sources.name: Tokyo International Film Festival – award winners

reports.subject: film
reports.headline: Filmin adds “Duse”, by Pietro Marcello, about the great stage actress, tomorrow, and Hlynur Pálmason's “The Love That Remains” on the 27th
reports.deck: Friday 6 also brings “Barrio Triste” and the documentary “Broken English”; later come “The Great Forger”, “Mala bèstia” and a new season of “Carmen Curlers”.
paragraphs: Filmin puts “Eleonora Duse, la divina” (“Duse”), by Pietro Marcello, in its Spanish catalogue on Friday 6 November. Valeria Bruni-Tedeschi plays the actress Eleonora Duse in her last years, returning to the stage despite fragile health, with Noémie Merlant as her daughter, Fausto Russo Alesi as D'Annunzio and Noémie Lvovsky as Sarah Bernhardt. The film (Italy and France, 2025, 122 minutes) competed at Venice and screened at last year's Seminci. Diego Lerer, at Micropsia, finds it melodramatic to the point of irritating some viewers, but coherent, with the weight resting on the performance and a stronger second half.

The same day brings “Barrio Triste”, Stillz's debut produced by Harmony Korine, about teenagers from Medellín's outskirts who steal a TV camera and roam the city, with music by Arca, and “Broken English”, Iain Forsyth and Jane Pollard's documentary on Marianne Faithfull. According to OtrosCines, Filmin also has “L'affaire Bojarski” (13 November), “Casi todo bien” (19), “Per te” and Bàrbara Farré's “Mala bèstia” (20), “Des preuves d'amour” and “Nuestro héroe, Balthazar” (26) and, on the 27th, Hlynur Pálmason's “The Love That Remains”.

For series, “Baron Noir” arrives on the 17th and season three of “Carmen Curlers” on the 24th per OtrosCines; a MarketingDirecto guide gives 10 November for the same season. The two sources disagree, so treat the date as one to confirm on Filmin. Dates are for Filmin Spain; we have not verified subtitles or how long titles stay up.

reports.subject: film
reports.headline: Criterion reveals January 2027: “Parasite” in 4K, “Deliverance”, Claire Denis's “Chocolat” and World Cinema Project Volume 6
reports.deck: A US edition; the article gives no exact dates or extras, and we cannot say how or when it will reach Spain.
paragraphs: According to The Film Stage (16 October), the Criterion Collection's January 2027 slate includes Claire Denis's “Chocolat” and Mike Leigh's “Career Girls” on Blu-ray; John Boorman's “Deliverance” in a new 4K edition with restored sound; Bong Joon-ho's “Parasite”, upgraded to 4K from the 2021 release; and “Midnight Cowboy”, brought back at full resolution for the first time since 2018.

World Cinema Project Volume 6, presented by Martin Scorsese, is a Blu-ray set of four recovered films: Flora Gomes's “Morta Nega” (Guinea-Bissau), Luis Sérgio Person's “São Paulo, Incorporated” (Brazil), Timité Bassori's “The Woman with the Knife” (Côte d'Ivoire) and Bahram Beyzai's “The Stranger and the Fog” (Iran). The article gives no release dates or extras; those are on Criterion's site. This is a US edition: disc region, Spanish or Catalan subtitles and distribution in Spain are unverified, so for now it would be an import.

sources.name: The Film Stage – Criterion January 2027 lineup

reports.subject: film
reports.headline: The Royal Ballet and Opera's “Carmen” by Damiano Michieletto reaches cinemas on 10 November; Spain unconfirmed
reports.deck: The distributor lists it as “international”; we can't tell whether it is live or a recording, and we found no new complete recording verified today.
paragraphs: Trafalgar Releasing gives 10 November 2026 for Bizet's “Carmen” in the Royal Ballet and Opera's cinema season, a revival of Damiano Michieletto's production with Sesto Quatrini conducting and Ginger Costa-Jackson and Russell Thomas as Carmen and Don José. OperaWire, in its 28 May article, agrees. Neither page says whether it is live or a recorded performance, nor gives runtime, language or subtitles.

The distributor's page says “countries available: international”, without naming Spain, and we found no Spanish cinema listing it. So we don't present it here as a verified offer. Some UK cinema listings give a different cast; check with the venue. A cinema screening is not a recommended complete recording, so we add no recording record. We found no other new complete theatre or opera recording with verified access from Spain today.

reports.headline: Calendar: “Duse” and the platforms on Friday 6, “Carmen” in cinemas on the 10th, and November at Filmin
reports.deck: Dates verified today, each with its territory; Friday 6 Spanish cinema releases are in yesterday's edition.
paragraphs: Thursday 5, in Spain, on Max: “Black Swan”, “The Whale”, “Jojo Rabbit”, “Cocktail”, “Constantine” and “The Color of Money”. On Movistar Plus+: “Día de caza”. Friday 6: “Duse”, “Barrio Triste” and “Broken English” on Filmin; “Wuthering Heights” on Movistar Plus+, and “Campus Drivers” on Prime Video. Sunday 8: season two of “City of God: The Fight Rages On” on Max. Tuesday 10: “Carmen” in cinemas (international; Spain unconfirmed).

Wednesday 11: “El cuerpo” on Netflix and season three of “The Rings of Power” on Prime Video. Thursday 12: classics on Max such as “1917” and “Little Miss Sunshine”. Friday 13: “L'affaire Bojarski” on Filmin. From the 19th to the 27th: “Casi todo bien”, “Mala bèstia”, “Des preuves d'amour” and, on the 27th, “The Love That Remains”, all on Filmin. All dates come from the platform guides cited; they may change.

reports.subject: film
reports.headline: Editor's picks: “Duse”, “Barrio Triste” and Michieletto's “Carmen” if it reaches a nearby screen
reports.deck: Editorial affinity, not a critics' or audience score.
paragraphs: “Duse” (Filmin, 6 November in Spain). Affinity 4 out of 5, medium confidence: a period biography about a stage actress, led by Bruni-Tedeschi. We haven't seen it; we rely on Diego Lerer's review, which highlights the performance and the second half and warns about the melodrama.

“Barrio Triste” (Filmin, 6 November in Spain). Affinity 3 out of 5, low confidence: a Colombian debut with a paranormal touch, judged from synopses only. Michieletto's “Carmen”, in cinemas on 10 November: affinity 4 out of 5 if it reaches Spain, which we couldn't confirm. And if you need opera, remember yesterday's edition: “Le Roi d'Ys” expires on Sunday at OperaVision.
The day in brief: few weighty news items, but a clear awards list in Tokyo and a Friday with theatre, period drama and auteur cinema on Filmin. On physical media, we wait for Criterion's exact dates.
